findings.description: Step 2 tells the reader to run `pup plan` to get the task's goal and scope-in, but `pup plan` only lists unclaimed backlog tasks, so a session that reads `awaiting-review` never appears in it.
findings.body:
Step 2 says "`pup plan` shows the task's goal and scope-in". The default `pup plan` verb is `list` (src/cli/index.ts:1308-1324). It prints one line per task from `listBacklogTasks` (src/core/session.repository.ts:151), which excludes tasks already claimed by a session. The other `pup plan` verbs are `add`, `drop` and `edit`, and none of them shows a claimed task. The skill runs only on a session that reads `awaiting-review`, and that session has already claimed its task. A console or conductor following the step will find nothing for the session, or an unrelated backlog.

`pup review <session>` already prints `goal:`, `scope-in:`, `scope-out:`, `acceptance:` and the ticket's slice criteria (src/cli/index.ts:2511-2519). So the `pup plan` clause adds nothing and misdirects.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/f5ee3dbd4aa0acf2dfb3dcad504adbff8ded616d/.claude/skills/review-session/SKILL.md#L27
findings.suggestion: `pup review <session>` prints the task's goal, scope-in, acceptance and the ticket's slice criteria (decision 187), then the file list. `gh issue view <n>` reads an issue the commit or the goal names. If there is no spec, the Spec subagent is skipped and the report says "no spec available".

findings.description: Step 2 says `pup review` prints the slice criteria and the file list unconditionally, but it prints criteria only when the spec carries a ticket (src/cli/index.ts:2518), and decision 187 notes that no command writes tickets yet, so most tasks print none.

Frontmatter sets disable-model-invocation: true but the description keeps a model-facing 'Use when a session reads awaiting-review and before pup merge --pr.' trigger sentence, and runs two sentences, where the repo's rule asks for a one-line human summary with trigger lists stripped.
